To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we have defined an operational semantics for an agent programming language that is expressive enough to serve as a foundation for agent communication languages; (ii) we have developed a simple abstract machine that interprets this language; and (iii) we have defined the operational semantics of a subset of the FIPA agent communication language ACL in terms of our language.
We present a formal semantics of an agent communication language, in the form of a set of operational transition rules.
we developed a basic multi-agent language with operational semantics that is based on a mental state model and that can be used as the basis for agent communication languages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a formal study of the operational aspects of agent communication languages, and with the design of abstract machines to interpret such languages.
a precise and formal specification of agent interaction and communication.

the development of a formal model that is expressive enough to capture the essential features of agent communication languages, and yet simple enough to be used in the design of a concrete implementation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have provided a formal semantics of the programming language that is both operational and compositional.
the semantics are defined by means, among other things, of transition rules that define the operational behaviour of the language.
the operational semantics is the formal semantics of the agent communication language.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed an agent communication language that is well-suited to the specification of complex multi-agent systems, that can be used to model the interaction between agents, that is well-suformed, and that is supported by a formal semantics.
we have defined an abstract machine for a multi-agent programming language, and that this machine is suitable for the implementation of agent communication languages.
we have defined a basic multi-agent language with a clear operational semantics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the operational semantics of the basic language are sufficiently expressive to accommodate the semantics of the main features of existing agent communication languages, such as FIPA-ACL and KAoS.
agent communication languages can benefit from a well-defined operational semantics that is grounded in a multi-agent programming language.
the operational semantics of a language for agent communication can be given in terms of a transition system, which can then be used as the basis for a compiler.
